scope: Bounded WebSocket presence-callback dispatch, per-user ordering, and shutdown behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release acceptance.
implemented: Ready callbacks are scheduled through a bounded dispatcher with at most 256 pending tickets and up to 8 workers.
Per-user callback completion is FIFO; callbacks for other users can run while a same-user predecessor is still active. Tests cover per-user order and progress under pool saturation.
Caller backpressure is bounded by the pending queue; callback event goroutines are not spawned per event. Submitters blocked on queue capacity are released on shutdown.

Workers exit after one idle second. Shutdown stops admission, cancels queued callbacks, and waits for active callbacks to return; active callbacks are not forcibly canceled and a callback that never returns can delay shutdown.
Hub visibility flags are synchronized, and conditional visibility commits reject stale callback results. Pre-registration flag handling was removed.

A callback that never returns cannot be canceled globally and may delay dispatcher shutdown. Most relevant callback operations use a five-second context, but this is not a hard cancellation guarantee for arbitrary callback code.
